picks.headline: News Summary: Survey Suggests Many Publishers Still Fail to Register Copyright
picks.excerpt: An Authors Guild survey found publishers had failed to register authors' copyrights, leaving some writers ineligible for the Anthropic settlement class — a paperwork failure that decides who gets paid when books are used as training data.
picks.rationale: The most actionable item in the pool: an unregistered copyright quietly disqualifies an author from AI settlement money, so every writer can check their own registration record tomorrow.

picks.headline: New manga platform features 300 titles translated into English for first time
picks.excerpt: Shueisha's Manga Million puts nearly 300 previously untranslated titles into English plus Spanish, French, Turkish and Polish — a translation volume no human-only pipeline has attempted, and one readers and letterers have publicly questioned over uncredited translators and machine output.
picks.rationale: A shipped localisation platform operating at a scale human-only pipelines cannot reach, which puts the translator-credit question in front of anyone working on multilingual publishing.

picks.headline: Is AI destroying the art and magic of children's books?
picks.excerpt: AI-generated 'slop' picture books are flooding online storefronts, and Creative Bloq talks to illustrators and parents about what happens to the craft of children's book illustration when generated art becomes the cheapest option. The piece looks at the tells of AI picture books and at the publishers and buyers trying to filter them out.
picks.rationale: Moves the AI-slop story from text to illustration and hands buyers and editors concrete tells for spotting a generated picture book.

picks.headline: Academic Publishers Develop Guidelines, Screening Tools for AI Use
picks.excerpt: Just as booksellers are inundated with AI slop and trade publishing reckons with suspicions of AI-written books, academic publishing is building vetting tools and author guidelines for AI use. Publishers Lunch argues the scholarly side's screening infrastructure can inform how trade houses handle submissions.
picks.rationale: Scholarly publishing already has the submission-screening playbook trade houses are improvising, which makes it a template an editor can borrow rather than another round of alarm.

picks.headline: Andrea Bartz Returns to Ballantine for AI-Inspired Thriller
picks.excerpt: Ballantine bought Delete Your Account by Andrea Bartz — the plaintiff in Bartz v. Anthropic — a novel about an author who has a chatbot write a book in the vein of her favourite thriller, with disastrous consequences.
picks.rationale: The lead plaintiff in the Anthropic training-data suit turns the fight into commercial fiction, a signal that generative AI is now saleable subject matter and not only a legal problem.
